newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH FINMIN SAYS OWED OVER CZK35BLN IN LATE TAXES.
newsitem.headline: CZECH FINMIN SAYS OWED OVER CZK35BLN IN LATE TAXES.

text.p: Czech tax arrears and penalties since 1993 exceeded 35 billion crowns at the end of last year, up from a total of 23 billion crowns at the end of 1995, Finance Minister Ivan Kocarnik said on Monday.

Kocarnik told a news conference that the figure equalled 3.6 percent of total tax collections in the period since sweeping reforms of the tax system were implemented in 1993, up from 3.3 percent at the end of 1995.
He said that an average of one quarter of arrears are never paid and that 60 percent of the total sum were unpaid taxes, while penalties on delays accounted for the remainder.
The minister blamed shortfalls in the business code for some arrears, which he called "speculative".

"Speculative insolvency...is the result of legal settlement which enables intentional shifting of tax duty subjects without sufficient property, and respectively, the creation of non-recoverable arrears," he told reporters.
